children: Our Bureau New Delhi: India's core sector output expanded to a series high of 7.9% year-on-year in September, driven by strong growth in coal, electricity, refinery products and iron ore, alongside a favourable base effect, official data released Wednesday showed. The growth stood at 5.9% in August and 3.1% in September 2025. "The core sector growth for September shows buoyancy in infrastructure where the government has been spending," said Madan Sabnavis, chief economist at Bank of Baroda. Expenditure on roads has boosted cement while railway outlay has fed into iron and steel output demand, he added.

Aditi Nayar, chief economist at ICRA, said core output growth was robust in September, the fastest pace in the new series, with a favourable base supporting the improvement. The September figures mark the fourth release under the revised index with 2022-23 as the new base year, replacing 2011-12. The updated series also includes iron ore, taking the number of core industries to nine.

Refinery products recorded their strongest growth in the new series, rising 10.3% year-on-year in September, up from 5.6% in August. "Rise in refinery output indicates heightened industrial activity as demand for fuel increased, with exports also supporting growth," said Sabnavis. Coal production rebounded sharply to a 13-month high of 10.7% in September, following a contraction of 3.8% in the previous month. Iron ore output growth also rose to 18.4% compared with 5.5%. "Coal and iron ore output witnessed a meaningful pickup in their year-on-year growth rates in September compared with August. While this was aided by a low base, the sequential uptick in coal was quite strong, amid low stocks at power plants," said Nayar.

title: Core Output Hits Series High of 7.9% in September
